holidays.name: National Absurdity Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate things that make no sense. Embrace the silly, the nonsensical and the delightfully illogical. Wear mismatched socks, hold a meeting in a funny hat, or ask a question that has no answer.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance with no clearly documented founder. It has become a popular fixture on fun-holiday calendars as a lighthearted excuse to loosen up.
holidays.funFact: Absurdism, the philosophy behind the idea, argues that humans keep searching for meaning in a universe that offers none. Its best-known champion, Albert Camus, said we should embrace that with a smile.

holidays.name: National Peanut Butter Fudge Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the rich, creamy, melt-in-your-mouth candy that is usually cut into small squares. Whip up a batch, trade a few pieces with neighbors, or just eat it straight from the pan.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It fits neatly into the season of holiday baking and candy-making.
holidays.funFact: Classic peanut butter fudge can be made in minutes with only a few ingredients, so it is one of the easiest candies for a beginner to try.

holidays.name: Name Your PC Day
holidays.description: A day to give your laptop or desktop computer a nickname. Whether it's Sir Crashalot or The Beast, a name turns a pile of circuits into a loyal office sidekick.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial tech observance with no well-documented founder. It grew out of the long tradition of people giving personalities to their gadgets.
holidays.funFact: Computers on a network need a unique name to be identified, so many IT teams have long named their machines after planets, Greek gods or cartoon characters.
